To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the contact angle for aqueous solutions of ionic surfactants depends on time and (2) the contact angle of aqueous solution of nonionic surfactants does not depend on time, but the contact angle of the pure water is higher than that of the solution.
the contact angle for the ionic surfactants on moderately hydrophobic polymers depends on time.
the wetting dynamics of ionic surfactants on polymer surfaces is strongly influenced by the ionic nature of surfactant, whereas the nonionic surfacts spread well on all the hydrophobes used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the unusual wetting dynamics of ionic and nonionic surfactants on polymer surfaces of varying hydrophobicity.
the wetting dynamics of surfactants in aqueous solutions and the influence of the substrate surface free energy.
the spreading of aqueous surfctant solutions on polymer substrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spreading of aqueous solutions on hydrophobic surfaces is controlled by the balance between the adsorption and desorption rates of the surfactant molecules.
the spreading of surfactant solutions over polymer surfaces is governed by the interplay of several factors.
the wetting dynamics is governed by a competition between diffusion of the surfactant to and adsorption of the surfactants at the liquid-vapor interface and adsorption at the solid-liquid interface.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamics of wetting of polymer surfaces by surfactant solutions is more complex than it was thought previously.
the spreading behavior of aqueous surfactive solutions on solid substrates is not as simple as previously believed.
the spreading dynamics of surfactant solutions is a complex process involving different mechanisms and depends not only on the nature of surfactants but also on the surface properties of the solid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the ionic surfactants, the contact angles of the solutions are strongly dependent on the concentration, the substrate hydrophobic/hydrophilic character, and the surfactant nature.
, for aqueous surfactants solutions, the wetting dynamics can be much more complex than that for the pure solvents.
the spreading of aqueous solutions on polymer substrates is a very complex process and that it is difficult to predict the final shape and size of the liquid drops on polymer surfaces.
